title: AZ traffic pinning & CNI connection-limit post-incident field report
content:
Short summary:
- Date/time: 2024-11-07 23:10 UTC — 2024-11-08 02:40 UTC (primary window)
- Impact: ~15% of pods in eu-west-1 AZ-b experienced long podStart latency (>30s) and transient connection failures to node-local proxies (istio sidecar + envoy). This manifested as API request timeouts for a subset of customer-facing routes and inflight request retries.
- Severity: Sev2 (customer-visible errors for subset of requests, not full region outage).
- Primary symptom: rapid rise in pod scheduling backoff combined with spikes in node-level TCP connection resets to local CNI agent.

Observed signals and dashboards:
- PodStart P99 for deployments in AZ-b jumped from 1.2s -> 42s around 23:10.
- kube-scheduler queue depth increased by ~600 pending pods (mostly low-priority batch/sidecar restarts).
- Node-level metric: conntrack entries per node peaked at ~1.4M on affected nodes (threshold ~1M).
- CNI metrics (calico-hosted): per-node conntrack-miss ratio rose and kernel conntrack reclamation thrashing observed.
- Etcd: healthy, no leader changes. Control plane latencies stayed within normal ranges.

Timeline (reconstructed):
- 23:05 UTC: Autoscaler triggers scale-up in several ASGs in AZ-b due to batch job churn. New nodes booting, kubelet registering.
- 23:10 UTC: First customer alert via synthetic monitors for increased 5xx. Internal alert "pod-start-surge-euw1-b" fires.
- 23:12 UTC: Oncall picks up. Early triage: high pod start latency + kubelet logs show "no available ephemeral ports" and "connection refused" to local iptables/CNI agent.
- 23:20 UTC: Observed CNI agent (calico-node) logs with repeated "failed to add iptables rule" and kernel OOM-like conntrack reclaims.
- 23:25 UTC: Team investigates host-level conntrack exhaustion. Attempts: increasing conntrack_max via sysctl on a couple of nodes as test (temporary). Noted immediate reduction in local errors but other nodes still thrashing.
- 23:40 UTC: Identified a correlated deploy in AZ-b: a new sidecar image that changed downstream keepalive behavior (short TCP timeouts + aggressive reconnects) was deployed to ~2k pods (canary->prod by rollout policy).
- 00:05 UTC: Rollback of that rollout started (linear rollback per deployment). Simultaneously, SRE increases cluster-wide conntrack_max via daemonset (sysctl).
- 00:35 UTC: PodStart latency begins to fall; kube-scheduler queue drains slowly. By 02:40 UTC, metrics back to baseline; post-incident work continues.

Root cause hypothesis (multi-factor):
1) Application-level change (aggresive sidecar reconnect) increased ephemeral TCP connection churn from clients to local proxies.
2) AZ-b had a higher density of pending restarts due to concurrent autoscaler activity, so per-node conntrack pressure was higher than typical.
3) Conntrack_max kernel setting on majority of older node images was conservative for this workload (default 65536 / tuned low).
4) CNI dataplane (iptables + calico) reacts poorly when conntrack is thrashing; timed operations to modify iptables rules started failing transiently which blocked pod networking setup and caused kubelet podStart stalls.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- Emergency rollback of the sidecar image rollout (rolled back to previous tag within 25 minutes for all impacted deployments).
- Cluster-wide conntrack increase: applied sysctl via DaemonSet to raise net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max from 65536 -> 262144 as a stopgap.
- Applied a temporary admission controller patch to delay new canary rollouts in AZ-b for 2h (block merge triggers).
- Cleaned conntrack state on the most severely impacted nodes (conntrack -F) as part of controlled remediation windows; limited to nodes with high pod churn to avoid collateral sessions loss.

Why the rollout triggered escalation:
- Rollout used per-deployment linear increases but many microservices share the same node pools; combined effect produced burst load on node conntrack table across thousands of pods in the same AZ and overlapping time window.
- Lack of an early detector for conntrack growth meant only downstream symptoms were visible (podStart and 5xx).

Post-incident analysis & proposed long-term actions (PRIORITIZED):
1) Technique: Introduce conntrack headroom policy in cluster autoscaler/launch configuration
   - Ensure new node images have nf_conntrack_max increased as default for node pools that host high-churn workloads.
   - Owner: infra-node (Mateo). ETA: 3 weeks (image bake + launch config rollout).
2) Monitoring: Add conntrack utilization alerting per AZ and per-node pool (p95 > 60% for 5m)
   - Alert -> paging, and a non-pager signal to SRE with runbook link. Owner: observability (Priya). ETA: 1 week.
3) Admission controls / rollout policy improvements:
   - Add cluster-level guard to limit concurrent rollout rate across node pools sharing an AZ (global concurrency cap).
   - Enforce default rolling update pauses when restart churn in same AZ > threshold. Owner: product-platform (Evan). ETA: 4 weeks.
4) Runbook additions (this doc is a draft):
   - Add step-by-step commands to check conntrack table, sysctls, calico/iptables failure patterns, and safe conntrack flush steps. Owner: Rina. ETA: now (this week).
5) Test & chaos engineering:
   - Schedule a game-day to inject connection churn in a staging AZ to exercise conntrack thresholds and guardrails. Owner: SRE-ops. ETA: 6 weeks.
6) Application-level: coordinate with platform and service owners to add TCP keepalive/backoff guidance into the sidecar SDK docs. Owner: platform-eng. ETA: 3 weeks.

Runbook draft (triage checklist, abbreviated):
- Detect:
  * dashboards: podStart p99 > 10s in single AZ OR node conntrack entries per node > 750k
  * logs: calico-node error patterns: "failed to add iptables rule"; kubelet: "failed to setup network for pod"
- Triage steps:
  1) Identify cluster/az/nodepool hotspots: use k8s label filters and aggregated node metrics.
  2) Check for concurrent rollouts: github/argoCD events in last 30m for those namespaces.
  3) Run on a problem node (SSH):
     - sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
     - sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
     - sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
     - journalctl -u calico-node -n 500 --no-pager | grep -i "error\|fail" -n
  4) If conntrack_count / max > 0.8 and errors present:
     - Schedule controlled conntrack flush on <one> node to observe impact. Command: sudo conntrack -F
     - If sidecar upstream is stateful and session loss unacceptable, prefer sysctl increase first. Command: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144 (and persist via sysctl.d config via daemonset).
  5) If iptables modification errors continue: cordon + drain problematic node and recreate.
- Recovery verification:
  * podStart p99 returns to baseline for 15m; kube-scheduler queue drains; calico error rate drops to near zero.

Testing and follow-ups (action items, owners):
- (High) Bake new node image with conntrack_max bump and updated calico version. Owner: infra-node / Mateo. Due: 2024-11-28.
- (High) Add conntrack alarms and a dashboard card by AZ. Owner: observability / Priya. Due: 2024-11-14.
- (Medium) Implement rollout concurrency cap across same-AZ deployments (proposal in RFC). Owner: product-platform / Evan. Due: 2024-12-12.
- (Low) Add developer guideline for TCP keepalive behavior in sidecar SDK; include recommended QPS/backoff parameters. Owner: platform-eng. Due: 2024-12-05.

Notes from investigation (raw snippets):
- Local conntrack view from node ip-10-0-12-44:
  * conntrack_count: 1,234,987
  * conntrack_max: 65536 (surprising — flagged nodes were running older kernel tunables)
  * calico logs: repeated "error: iptables command failed with exit status 2" -> indicates concurrent iptables edits.
- We saw a pattern where repeated reconnects created ephemeral sockets faster than conntrack GC could reclaim them; netfilter GC then started synchronous reclaims causing CPU spikes on netfilter path.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why were node images out of sync on conntrack_max? Image bake pipeline expected to standardize. Is there drift in ASG launch configs?
- Is our conntrack GC behavior predictable with current calico version? Could an upstream calico kernel interaction be improved by an upgrade?
- Do we want to introduce a global circuit-breaker for rollouts, or prefer per-service backpressure?

Quick links:
- Jira: SRE-7213 (incident)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-config/pull/428 (daemonset sysctl + monitoring dashboards)
- Slack thread: #sre-ops 2024-11-07 (use Slack search for "conntrack" around event)

Appendix: quick commands cheat-sheet (for runbook)
- View conntrack count: sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
- View max: sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
- Increase temporarily: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
- Persist via daemonset: echo "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144" > /etc/sysctl.d/99-nf_conntrack.conf && sysctl --system
- Flush conntrack (use cautiously): sudo conntrack -F
- Check calico logs: journalctl -u calico-node -n 500 --no-pager | grep -i "iptables\|conntrack\|error"

Draft end — this is intentionally conversational. Feedback welcome: annotate in the doc or ping @Rina in #sre-ops.
